notes:
T295 context dump — acceptance runner PATH fix.

Read: AGENTS.md, DELEGATEE.md, managent spec.md (§done), T295 brief (untracked/T295-acceptance-runner-path.md), src/managent/main.zig (full), std lib Threaded.zig (init/spawn/scanEnviron), std lib process.zig (run/SpawnOptions), tools/regression-managent-integrity.sh, tools/smoke.sh, build.zig, findings-schema.json.

Root cause identified: main.zig line 140 initializes Threaded IO with empty InitOptions. InitOptions.environ defaults to .empty. Threaded.environ_initialized is set true because block.isEmpty() is true, so scanEnviron() is a no-op. spawnPosix uses t.environ.process_environ.createPosixBlock() which creates an empty env block. All child processes get zero environment variables.

Fix applied:
1. main.zig:140 — pass init.environ to Threaded.init (one line)
2. main.zig cmdDone — distinguish CANNOT RUN (infrastructure fault) from ACCEPTANCE FAILED (task failure) using exit codes 127/126 and spawn errors
3. main.zig cmdAudit — add WARN finding for done tasks with skip_acceptance_reason (surfaces bypassed acceptance checks)
4. tools/smoke.sh — staleness changed from FAIL to STALE (exit 0, loud warning) — §5 ruling option 3
5. tools/regression-managent-integrity.sh — git init instead of touch .git (pre-existing test bug exposed by env fix), plus checks 14-16 for T295 controls

All 16 integrity checks pass. zig build test passes (exit 0).

Could not establish: whether the integrity test was already red before T295 (the 'cannot ask git' REJECTED path in cmdDone). The pre-existing touch .git created a non-repo, but with no PATH the old binary couldn't find git → gitOk returned false → REJECTED. If the test was already red, it was invisible because --build wasn't used routinely. The git init fix makes it moot.

Did not act on: other potential environment-dependent behavior in managent (runCommand, runGit, claimlint spawning, standing trigger spawning) — the single Threaded.init fix covers all of them since they all go through the same io.

Assumed without checking: that changing staleness from FAIL to STALE in smoke.sh would not break zig build test's wire-in (it doesn't — smoke.sh exit 0 on staleness, which is fine for a test dependency).

Noticed but did not act on: bin/managent and zig-out/bin/managent had different SHAs after build (1,035,392 vs 1,017,240 bytes) despite same version stamp — this is the codesign/rm-cp dance; deploy.sh should have made them identical but they differ. Possibly the build.zig deploy step and the manual deploy.sh interact oddly. The integrity test's stamp check looks at version strings, not binary hashes — a known limitation of the stamping approach (T268).
